title: A law recognizes its space rather than creating it
claim: (1) Systems with the same allowed states have the same circuits, knots, knot matroid and readings. (2) A parity law's knot matroid is the column matroid M[C] of its direction code C. (3) A gauge law over any group with at least two elements has the cycles of its graph as circuits (knot matroid M(G)); a Tseitin law has the bonds (M*(G)). (4) For a 3-connected graph, the minimal supports of the cut space whose deletion leaves the matroid connected are exactly the vertex stars, so the allowed states determine the graph; two graphs on one edge set have identical allowed states exactly when they are 2-isomorphic (Whitney), so a twist changes the graph but not the states. (5) For a 3-connected planar graph the dual reading returns the face boundaries of its unique embedding, and the read cells form the 2-sphere. (6) For a parity law whose knot matroid M is 3-connected with at least 4 elements, the reading succeeds exactly when M is graphic and then returns the unique graph whose translated gauge states are the law's; the dual reading succeeds exactly when M is cographic; both exactly when the graph is planar; by Tutte, failure is witnessed by an F7, F7*, M*(K5) or M*(K3,3) minor. (7) So within parity laws a space is recognized, not created: it is read from the allowed states alone and present exactly when the knot matroid is graphic; a local law of 8 random constraints on 16 variables, written on no graph, carries a sphere, and almost every balanced random code carries no graph. Cited remark: on a locally finite infinite graph the Tseitin circuits are the minimal finite cuts with a finite side over all solutions, and the finite bonds within one class of finitely different solutions, whose dual (Bruhn and Diestel) has the circles through the ends as circuits.
failure_conditions: A coset of a binary code has a circuit that is not a minimal support of the dual code with at least two elements, or conversely.
A gauge law over a group with at least two elements has a circuit that is not a cycle, or a Tseitin law a circuit that is not a bond.
The reading of a 3-connected graph's gauge states is not its star family, or a Whitney twist changes the allowed states.
A 3-connected planar graph's readings fail, or do not give a connected complex with every edge in two faces, every vertex link one cycle and V - E + F = 2.

A binary code is not spanned by its minimal supports, the reading succeeds on F7, F7*, M*(K5) or M*(K3,3) or fails on M(K5) or M(K3,3), or on a 3-connected code the reading disagrees with an exhaustive search for a graph realization.
A control ('reading from all minimal supports', 'the allowed states determine the graph exactly', 'the reading needs no 3-connectivity', 'a law written on no graph carries none') is accepted.
foundation_claim_scope: What a law's allowed states determine about the graph or surface it is written on. No native recurrence, composed topology in the protected sense, path, metric distance, physical space or dimension claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py verifies the parity lemma on 40 random cosets, gauge circuits over Z2, Z3, Z4 and S3 on 56 laws and Tseitin circuits on 14, recovery of 30 random 3-connected graphs and 8 Whitney twists, spheres (faces, vertex links, Euler count) on 12 planar graphs and the sphere law, the minors F7, F7*, M*(K5), M*(K3,3), agreement of the reading with an exhaustive realization search on 40 random 3-connected codes and on the 13 three-connected local laws of the census; four controls rejected; no human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with exhaustive and randomized checks; classical theorems of Whitney and Tutte cited; the infinite remark rests on HOLES-AT-INFINITY-20261020-001B-P001 and Bruhn-Diestel and is not checked; no trusted kernel.
validation.novelty: known: the mathematics is classical (Whitney 1932-33, Tutte 1958-59 and 1963, Bruhn-Diestel); the delta is the reading of knot matroids as the space a law carries: presentation invariance, the gauge-Tseitin duality as knot-matroid duality, a randomly written local law carrying a sphere, and the two infinite readings.
